identification: Gill cover with 3-5 distinct bony striae radiating downward (FNAM, DORIS, IEO).
Pelvic fin origin well behind the dorsal fin origin; last two anal rays enlarged (FNAM, DORIS).
Terminal mouth, jaws not extending past the eye (DORIS, IEO).
Green/olive back, silvery flanks, with one to three rows of dark spots along the upper flanks (FNAM, IEO).
Belly with scutes but not sharply keeled (FNAM).
similar: Sprat Sprattus sprattus: pelvic fins in front of or under the dorsal origin (DORIS).
Young shads Alosa spp.: also striated gill cover, but sardine has the last two anal rays enlarged and the mouth ending before the eye centre (DORIS).
Anchovy: prominent snout, mouth split far behind the eye (DORIS).
Sardinella: yellow longitudinal line along the flank (DORIS); herring: small firmly attached scales, pelvics before the dorsal (DORIS).
anglingMethods: No rod-and-line method documented in fetched sources; taken commercially by purse seine and pelagic trawl (DORIS, IEO guide).
conservation: IUCN Red List: Least Concern (assessed 2013; FishBase). EU minimum conservation reference size 11 cm in South-Western Waters (Reg. 2019/1241 Annex VII, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2019/1241/annex/VII/adopted); IEO guide and DORIS also give 11 cm. Gulf of Cadiz purse-seine fishery under a national management plan (BOE).

habitat: Neritic pelagic schooling fish between the coast and shelf edge; euryhaline (5-41 ppt), entering lagoons and estuaries, especially to spawn and as juveniles.

size.maxNote: 20 cm SL maximum; common 13.5 cm SL (FishBase, IEO); FNAM usually 12-15 cm.

diet: Mesozooplankton, mainly calanoid copepods, plus crustacean and mollusc larvae and fish eggs.
behaviour: Large, often mixed-species schools in constant motion; daily vertical migration (deeper and grouped by day, dispersed near the surface at night); moves north and into surface waters in summer, retreats and descends in winter.
seasonal: Bay of Biscay spawning March-August, peak May-June at 14-18 C surface temperature, with key areas offshore of the Gironde and Adour estuaries and shelf-edge upwellings (DORIS; FNAM: April-August, through October on the Biscay coast). Gulf of Cadiz: larvae/early juveniles abundant in the Guadalquivir estuary in summer (Miró et al., reported by Ecoticias 2020).

gironde.basis: DORIS: key Bay of Biscay spawning area offshore of the Gironde estuary; 382 EVHOE records in the Gironde box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427).

biscay.basis: 835 EVHOE records in the French Biscay box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427); DORIS: Bay of Biscay spawning, 12 cm French minimum size, pair-trawl/purse-seine fishery.

cantabria.basis: IEO guide: purse-seine target with names 'anchoa, bocarte' in Asturias and Cantabria (https://diversimar.cesga.es/docus/Guia_Especies.pdf); 130 larval records in RADIALES (https://obis.org/dataset/e4a8170e-2176-4124-9c97-911c04c3bf2f).

galicia.basis: Listed for Galicia by Bañón & Maño 2021 (https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/nacc/article/view/7198/10694); IEO Galician names 'bocareu, bocarte, anxova'.

portugal.basis: Listed for mainland Portugal as 'Biqueirão' (Carneiro et al. 2014, https://europeanjournaloftaxonomy.eu/index.php/ejt/article/download/196/318).

cadiz.basis: Most abundant fish larva/juvenile in all zones of four Gulf of Cadiz estuaries, highest in the Guadalquivir (Miró et al., Sci. Total Environ., reported at https://www.ecoticias.com/naturaleza/204980_turbidez-guadalquivir-potencia-produccion-boquerones-estuario); main purse-seine target with an ICES IX quota (BOE, https://boe.es/boe/dias/2014/03/14/pdfs/BOE-A-2014-2738.pdf).

identification: Pointed snout projecting well beyond the lower jaw; mouth inferior with the upper jaw reaching far behind the eye (FNAM, DORIS).
Single short dorsal fin; anal fin behind the dorsal base (FNAM).
Silver lateral band edged above by a dark line; back blue-green fading quickly to grey (FNAM).
Belly rounded, without keeled scutes; scales shed very easily (FNAM).
Large eye set far forward (DORIS).
similar: Sardine: terminal mouth, dorsal fin further forward, spots on flanks (DORIS).
Sprat: superior mouth (DORIS); herring: small adherent scales (DORIS).
Sand smelt Atherina presbyter: two dorsal fins (IEO, DORIS).
Sardinella: yellow longitudinal line and deeper body (DORIS).
anglingMethods: No rod-and-line method documented in fetched sources; commercial pelagic pair trawl (~80% of French catch) and purse seine (DORIS, IEO).
conservation: IUCN Red List: Least Concern (assessed 2013; FishBase; DORIS notes the assessment described declines). EU minimum conservation reference size 12 cm (or 90 per kg), but 9 cm in ICES sub-area 9 (Reg. 2019/1241 Annex VII, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2019/1241/annex/VII/adopted). DORIS: French Bay of Biscay fishery closed 2005-2010 after a collapse. IEO guide (citing older Reg. 850/98): 10 cm south of Fisterra, 12 cm elsewhere in the Cantabrian-NW ground.

habitat: Pelagic-neritic schooling fish, usually over sandy bottoms at 100-200 m but also near the surface and in coastal waters; can descend to over 1,000 m, notably in winter.

size.maxNote: 70 cm TL maximum (FishBase; IEO gives 70 cm FL); common 22 cm FL (FishBase); FNAM: to about 60 cm FL, common to 30 cm; DORIS: 30-40 cm.

behaviour: Gregarious, forming large schools; hunts in schools, more active at night; daily vertical migration (near surface at night, near bottom by day); juveniles shelter under jellyfish.
seasonal: Western stock spawns from the Bay of Biscay to Ireland in (early) spring, then moves north and east (FishBase, DORIS). Comes closer to shore in summer (DORIS). British Sea Fishing: within shore range in warm summer months, most active at sunset.

gironde.basis: 521 EVHOE records plus 28 egg-survey records in the Gironde box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427).

biscay.basis: 4,540 EVHOE records and ~1,800 egg records (ICES egg surveys) in the French Biscay box; FishBase: western stock spawns off Biscay.

cantabria.basis: IEO guide: trawl and purse-seine target ('chicharro, jurel') (https://diversimar.cesga.es/docus/Guia_Especies.pdf); ~5,000 ICES egg-survey records in the Cantabria box.

galicia.basis: Bañón & Maño 2021: species of high commercial interest in Galicia (https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/nacc/article/view/7286/10671); IEO Galician names 'chicharro, chincho, xurelo'.

portugal.basis: Listed for mainland Portugal as 'Carapau' (Carneiro et al. 2014, https://europeanjournaloftaxonomy.eu/index.php/ejt/article/download/196/318); >1,000 ICES egg-survey records in the Portugal box.

cadiz.basis: 154 ICES mackerel/horse-mackerel egg-survey records in the Cadiz box (OBIS, https://api.obis.org/v3/occurrence?scientificname=Trachurus+trachurus&geometry=POLYGON%28%28-7.4+35.95%2C-5.6+35.95%2C-5.6+37.3%2C-7.4+37.3%2C-7.4+35.95%29%29&size=0); 'jureles (Trachurus spp.)' authorised purse-seine species in the Gulf of Cadiz plan (https://boe.es/boe/dias/2014/03/14/pdfs/BOE-A-2014-2738.pdf).

identification: Enlarged scute-like scales along the whole lateral line (bayonet-shaped course), 66-75 scales+scutes in total (FNAM, DORIS).
Dorsal accessory lateral line long, ending below soft dorsal rays 23-31 (FNAM; IEO).
Small black spot on the edge of the gill cover near its upper angle; very large eye (FNAM, DORIS).
Two dorsal fins; two detached spines before the anal fin (DORIS).
Back dark grey/blue-green, lower two-thirds silvery; caudal dirty yellow (IEO).
similar: Mediterranean horse mackerel T. mediterraneus: accessory lateral line ends below the 8th spine to 3rd soft dorsal ray; 75-89 scales+scutes; often yellowish fins (FNAM, DORIS).
Blue jack mackerel T. picturatus: accessory lateral line ends below soft dorsal rays 5-10; 93-100 scales+scutes; slender, dark blue back, offshore (FNAM, DORIS).
From a distance: bogue Boops boops or Atlantic mackerel (DORIS).
anglingMethods: Mostly taken on feathers, 'daylights' or other small lures, best around sunset; comes within shore range in warm summer months (British Sea Fishing - scad, https://britishseafishing.co.uk/scad/).
conservation: IUCN Red List (global): Vulnerable, A2bd (assessed 2013; FishBase). EU minimum conservation reference size 15 cm, with up to 5% 12-15 cm allowed (Reg. 2019/1241 Annex VII, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2019/1241/annex/VII/adopted); DORIS cites a French 15 cm minimum (arrêté of 19 March 2007).

habitat: Warm-water pelagic-neritic schooling fish, epipelagic to mesodemersal; enters brackish water.

size.maxNote: 55 cm TL maximum (FishBase); IEO guide and FNAM give 50 cm FL max and 30 cm FL common.

diet: Zooplankton when young; larger fish increasingly eat cephalopods, crustaceans and small pelagic fish (anchovy, sardine, sprat).
behaviour: Schooling and strongly migratory (FNAM); often caught as by-catch of sardine/anchovy purse seines and pelagic trawls.
seasonal: No region-specific seasonality found. FNAM: common north to the Bay of Biscay, occasional individuals further north.

gironde.basis: 12 EVHOE records in the Gironde box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427); within FNAM range ('commonly north to the Bay of Biscay', https://fishes-fnam.linnaeus.naturalis.nl/linnaeus_ng/app/views/species/taxon.php?id=109703).

biscay.basis: 177 EVHOE records in the French Biscay box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427); FNAM: common north to the Bay of Biscay.

galicia.basis: Listed for Galicia by Bañón & Maño 2021 (older records as S. japonicus) (https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/nacc/article/view/7286/10671); IEO Galician name 'xarda'.

portugal.basis: Listed for mainland Portugal as 'Cavala' (Carneiro et al. 2014, https://europeanjournaloftaxonomy.eu/index.php/ejt/article/download/196/318).

cadiz.basis: Age and growth study on Gulf of Cadiz samples from the Andalusian fleet and surveys (Velasco et al. 2011, https://www.redalyc.org/pdf/479/47919219004.pdf); described as a commercial species in the Gulf of Cadiz (Rivas-Mena et al. 2024, https://produccioncientifica.uca.es/documentos/65d1e689824cc36763f8c39c?lang=en).

identification: Swim bladder present (FNAM, IEO).
Belly marked with broken wavy lines or spots (FNAM; British Sea Fishing: many small spots on lower flanks).
Large eye (IEO, British Sea Fishing).
First dorsal with 8-10 spines; space between the dorsal fins about equal to the first-dorsal groove (FNAM; IEO: barely longer than the first dorsal).
Back greenish with fine, faint wavy bands; second dorsal and anal yellowish (IEO).
similar: Atlantic mackerel Scomber scombrus: no swim bladder, plain unspotted belly, bolder/thicker dark wavy bars, gap between dorsal fins about 1.5 times the first dorsal length (IEO, British Sea Fishing).
anglingMethods: Taken on spinners, daylights and feathers, usually incidentally while fishing for Atlantic mackerel (British Sea Fishing - Spanish mackerel, https://britishseafishing.co.uk/spanish-mackerel/).
conservation: IUCN Red List: Least Concern (assessed 2022; FishBase). EU minimum conservation reference size 20 cm for Scomber spp. in South-Western Waters (Reg. 2019/1241 Annex VII, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2019/1241/annex/VII/adopted); IEO guide: 20 cm in the Cantabrian-NW ground.

habitat: Epipelagic, neritic schooling fish mostly in coastal waters over the continental shelf, near the surface; may enter estuaries; tolerates 12-27 C and salinity 14-39.

size.maxNote: 91.4 cm FL maximum, 11 kg max published weight; common 50 cm FL (FishBase, ICCAT, IEO).

diet: Mainly small schooling fishes (anchovy, sardine and other clupeoids, gadoids, mackerels), also squid and shrimp; cannibalistic; daytime predator.
behaviour: Gregarious, schools of a few to several hundred fish near the surface, sometimes mixed with tunas, amberjacks and jacks; long coastal migrations (average ~2.6 km/day).
seasonal: Seasonal migrations, approaching coasts in summer (DORIS). Spawning does not occur in northern European waters (FNAM). Migrates along the coast from the Atlantic into the Alboran Sea to spawn and back (ICCAT). Autumn records on the French Biscay shelf (EVHOE survey, Oct-Nov).

gironde.basis: 19 EVHOE (autumn survey) records in the Gironde box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427); seasonal coastal presence per DORIS/FNAM.

biscay.basis: 53 EVHOE (autumn) records in the French Biscay box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427); FNAM: no spawning in northern European waters; DORIS: summer inshore migration.

galicia.basis: Listed for Galicia by Bañón & Maño 2021 (https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/nacc/article/view/7286/10671); seasonality inferred from DORIS/FNAM.

portugal.basis: Listed for mainland Portugal as 'Sarrajão' (Carneiro et al. 2014, https://europeanjournaloftaxonomy.eu/index.php/ejt/article/download/196/318); seasonality not documented.

cadiz.basis: Authorised purse-seine species in the Gulf of Cadiz plan (BOE, https://boe.es/boe/dias/2014/03/14/pdfs/BOE-A-2014-2738.pdf); ICCAT describes coastal migration between the Atlantic and the Alboran Sea through the Strait (https://www.iccat.int/Documents/SCRS/Manual/CH2/2_1_10_1_BON_ENG.pdf).

identification: 5-11 dark, slightly oblique stripes on the back running forward and downward (FNAM, DORIS, IEO).
Very long first dorsal fin with 20-23 spines and a straight edge; the two dorsals almost touching (FNAM, DORIS).
7-9 dorsal and 6-8 anal finlets (DORIS).
Large, widely split mouth (DORIS); strong median caudal keel between two smaller keels (IEO).
Back and upper sides steel blue, belly silvery (FNAM, IEO).
similar: Skipjack Katsuwonus pelamis: stripes only on the belly (DORIS).
Little tunny Euthynnus alletteratus: wavy marks only on the rear of the back and dark spots between pectoral and pelvic fins (DORIS, ICCAT).
Bullet tuna Auxis rochei: dorsal fins widely separated (IEO).
Young tunas: uniform dark back without stripes (DORIS).
anglingMethods: Troll lines ('curricán') are the gear listed for it in the Cantabrian-NW guide (https://diversimar.cesga.es/docus/Guia_Especies.pdf).

A French tackle retailer describes spinning with small jigs (10-45 g), pencil lures and jerkbaits, trolling and chumming from an anchored boat for 'bonito', but does not state which species it means (https://www.leurredelapeche.fr/es/articles/131-donde-pescar-bonito-como-pescar-bonito.html) - low reliability.
conservation: IUCN Red List: Least Concern (assessed 2021; FishBase). IEO guide: no minimum size ('sin regular') in the Cantabrian-NW ground (https://diversimar.cesga.es/docus/Guia_Especies.pdf). Managed under ICCAT as a small tuna.

habitat: Epipelagic, neritic tuna of inshore waters, more coastal than other tunas; near shoals, offshore islands, swift currents, thermal fronts and upwellings; warm water (most abundant at 24-30 C in the tropics).

size.maxNote: 122 cm TL maximum and 16.5 kg (FishBase; ICCAT: 122 cm FL reported for the Mediterranean). ICCAT: maximum 80.6 cm FL reported for the Northeast Atlantic.

diet: Opportunistic predator of crustaceans, small fishes (mainly clupeoids), squids, heteropods and tunicates.
behaviour: Schools by size, scattering at certain times of year; less migratory than larger tunas; large schools signalled by diving birds.
seasonal: Rare north of the Iberian Peninsula (FNAM, ICCAT). North Atlantic spawning period April-November (ICCAT). No region-specific seasonality found.

galicia.basis: Bañón & Maño 2021 class the only Galician record (Solórzano et al. 1983, 'rarely seen') as doubtful (https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/nacc/article/view/7286/10671).

cadiz.basis: Authorised purse-seine species ('bacoreta') in the Gulf of Cadiz plan (BOE, https://boe.es/boe/dias/2014/03/14/pdfs/BOE-A-2014-2738.pdf); ICCAT cites biological studies of fish from the Atlantic area near the Strait and the southern Iberian Peninsula (https://www.iccat.int/Documents/SCRS/Manual/CH2/2_1_10_5_LTA_ENG.pdf); seasonality not documented.

identification: Complex wavy/broken dark striped pattern on the back, not extending forward beyond the middle of the first dorsal fin (FNAM, ICCAT; DORIS photo: irregular pattern on the rear two-thirds of the back).
Several dark spots between the pectoral and pelvic fins, not always conspicuous (FNAM, ICCAT, DORIS).
Two dorsal fins separated by a narrow space; anterior first-dorsal spines tall, giving a strongly concave outline (ICCAT).

identification: Two dorsal fins separated by a large gap at least equal to the first-dorsal base (ICCAT, IEO).
Corselet scales form a wide band behind the pectoral: more than 6 (usually 10-15) scales wide under the second-dorsal origin (ICCAT, FNAM).
15 or more fairly broad, nearly vertical dark bars on the scaleless area above the lateral line (FNAM, ICCAT).

habitat: Epipelagic, neritic; diurnal coastal fish living in loose groups close to the surface; sometimes moves far up rivers.

size.maxNote: 104 cm TL maximum (FishBase); common 45 cm SL (FishBase, IEO). FNAM: to 62 cm body length (~90 cm SL) for B. b. belone, ~70 cm SL for B. b. gracilis; DORIS: 30 cm to over 1 m, up to 5 kg.

diet: Small fishes (sandeels, anchovy, sprat, sardine and other clupeids), plus crustaceans, worms and plankton; seizes prey sideways in the beak.
behaviour: Young form large schools, adults small scattered groups near the surface; fast swimmer that leaps when hooked or chased by tunas; attracted to lights at night; migrates like mackerel.

gironde.basis: DORIS (French coasts): inshore spring-summer and may move up rivers; 1 EVHOE record in the Gironde box (https://obis.org/dataset/34fa67d9-6100-47c6-a264-45ee6a54b427); no estuary-specific record found.

biscay.basis: DORIS seasonal pattern for French coasts (https://doris.ffessm.fr/Especes/Belone-belone-Orphie-commune-1031); museum and iNaturalist records in the French Biscay box via OBIS.

cantabria.basis: IEO guide species file (purse seine; minimum size 30 cm in Asturias, 25 cm elsewhere; Asturias 'agujachínfano', Cantabria 'aguja') (https://diversimar.cesga.es/docus/Guia_Especies.pdf); seasonality inferred from DORIS, not regional.

galicia.basis: Listed for Galicia by Bañón & Maño 2021 (https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/nacc/article/view/7198/10694); IEO Galician names 'agulla, corcito'; seasonality inferred from DORIS.

portugal.basis: Listed for mainland Portugal as 'Agulha'/'Peixe-agulha' (Carneiro et al. 2014, https://europeanjournaloftaxonomy.eu/index.php/ejt/article/download/196/318); 84 OBIS records (Berlengas, NW Portugal ichthyoplankton); seasonality inferred from DORIS.

cadiz.basis: 'Aguja (Belone belone)' is an authorised purse-seine species in the Gulf of Cadiz plan (BOE, https://boe.es/boe/dias/2014/03/14/pdfs/BOE-A-2014-2738.pdf); FNAM range to Madeira/Canaries and the Mediterranean; seasonality inferred.

identification: Very slender body with long beak-like jaws (about twice head length) armed with sharp teeth; lower jaw slightly longer than upper (DORIS, IEO).
Single dorsal and anal fins set far back, opposite each other; deeply forked caudal (DORIS, IEO).
Back dark blue-green, flanks silvery, belly white (DORIS, IEO).
Jaw teeth comparatively large and widely spaced (6-15 per orbit length on mid upper jaw); vomerine teeth usually present in larger fish (FNAM).
Green bones (biliverdin) (DORIS, British Sea Fishing).
similar: Short-beaked garfish Belone svetovidovi: smaller (to ~57 cm SL), shorter beak, smaller closely spaced jaw teeth (13-21 per orbit length), no vomerine teeth, more gill rakers (38-52 vs 27-40), more compressed body and narrower interorbital (FNAM, DORIS, British Sea Fishing).
Atlantic saury Scomberesox saurus: finlets behind dorsal and anal fins, shorter jaws (IEO lists it as the look-alike).
Halfbeak Hemiramphus balao: smaller, dorsal and anal fins not aligned (DORIS).
anglingMethods: Spinning with thin silver spinners, feathers, daylights or soft lures near the surface from piers and breakwaters, or float fishing a mackerel belly strip (also herring/squid strip, small sandeel) 2-3 ft deep on a size 4-8 hook; groundbait helps; bottom baits do not work (British Sea Fishing, https://britishseafishing.co.uk/garfish/).
Attracted to lights at night and leaps when hooked (DORIS, FishBase).
conservation: IUCN Red List: Least Concern (assessed 2012; FishBase). IEO guide: minimum size 30 cm in Asturias and 25 cm in the rest of the Cantabrian-NW ground (https://diversimar.cesga.es/docus/Guia_Especies.pdf). No EU minimum size in Annex VII.

size.maxNote: 140 cm TL maximum and 15 kg (FishBase, IEO); FNAM: to 120 cm SL, usually 30-70 cm.
